[USER] The user is thinking of creating a content calendar to help stay organized.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A content calendar is an excellent way to plan, organize, and streamline the content creation process.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested templates include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Basic Content Calendar Template: A simple Excel or Google Sheets template to plan content for the month.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - [Download Excel template](https://www.smartsheet.com/content-calendar-template)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - [Download Google Sheets template](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qk4uZJQ3RPLpZkGUc3sQwS2LQ3QwS2LQ3QwS2LQ/copy)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Content Calendar with Additional Columns: A more detailed template with columns for content type, target audience, keywords, and more.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - [Download Excel template](https://www.hubspot.com/blog/email-marketing/content-calendar-template)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - [Download Google Sheets template](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gX2gX2gX2gX2gX2gX2gX2gX2g/copy)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Monthly Content Calendar: A calendar view template to plan content for the month, including space for notes and deadlines.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - [Download PDF template](https://www.contentmarketinginstitute.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Content-Calendar-Template.pdf)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested tools include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Google Calendar  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Trello  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Asana  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. CoSchedule  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Hootsuite  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Airtable  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips to get started include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Choose a template or tool that fits your needs and comfort level.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Identify your content goals and objectives.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Plan your content in advance (at least 2-4 weeks).
